idiom_name: closed variant set + one type per legal shape + validating constructors + exhaustive consumption
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: enumerate the legal shapes of the value, give each shape its own type carrying only the fields that are meaningful there, and close the set so no further shape can be introduced. Make the constructors the only door - they validate the underlying primitives (or parse untrusted input) and return a failure value instead of building an illegal variant - and keep the fields private so nobody can assemble a shape by hand. Consume the value with an exhaustive match over the closed set, so a new shape becomes a compile-time error at every use site; where the language cannot close a set, the same discipline is enforced by opaque types, accessor functions, linters and review. Where the language offers the parts (enums, sealed hierarchies, discriminated unions, final classes with private constructors), let it enforce closure and exhaustiveness instead of relying on convention.
code_sketch:
legal_shapes = {Disconnected, Connecting(initiated), Connected(session_id)}
state = constructor(disconnected)            # only legal payloads are accepted
state = try_parse(untrusted_input)           # failure instead of an illegal value
match state:                                 # must handle every shape
    Disconnected -> ...
    Connecting(started) -> ...
    Connected(session_id) -> ...
pitfalls: Skipping the smart constructor and assembling variants from raw fields re-opens every illegal state the model was meant to exclude.
A wildcard or default arm in the consumer silently absorbs new variants, cancelling the guarantee exactly when the model grows.
Duplicating the model at the persistence or wire boundary creates a second, unchecked representation that can hold states the domain type forbids.

Wrong move: Force an evolving external enum into a closed union with no explicit unknown case -> a newly deployed value is rejected, discarded or misclassified, so forward compatibility fails -> instead retain an `Unknown`/unsupported boundary case and convert to the closed domain only after policy decides what it means.

Wrong move: Encode a context-dependent or cross-record rule as an absolute type invariant -> the model becomes brittle when requirements or external data change and cannot represent legitimate intermediate states -> instead keep stable local invariants in types and validate context-dependent rules at the boundary or at the operation that has the needed context.

Wrong move: Let reflection-based serialization or ORM hydration instantiate domain variants directly -> defaults and incomplete input can bypass validating constructors and masquerade as legal values -> instead deserialize into a transport shape and map through the domain constructor.
